title: P02 follow-up: RMS-matched Muon update scaling (Moonshot convention), which doubles only fc2's step, on the 070 incumbent
description: P02 follow-up (Muon update-scale convention): replaces Keller Jordan's sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) shape factor with sqrt(max(rows, cols)/D), the RMS-matched convention of Liu et al. (2025) with its constant folded into MUON_LR; Q/K/V, attention proj, fc1 and head are unchanged and only the (256, 1024) fc2 update doubles, with decay, LRs, batch 128, schedule and init identical to incumbent 070-claude. Under 10x decoupled decay each matrix's equilibrium norm tracks its update size, so the MLP residual write is currently held below the other writes by an orientation quirk; equalizing it tests whether stronger MLP writes give expert iteration a better starting policy.
hypothesis: Keller Jordan's Muon scales each orthogonalized update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)), so fc2 (256x1024, output narrower than input) gets element RMS ~1/32 while every other Muon matrix here (Q/K/V, proj, fc1, head) gets ~1/16. The spectral feature-learning condition (Yang, Simon & Bernstein 2023) would give fc2 less still (sqrt(fan_out/fan_in)=0.5); Moonshot's RMS matching (Liu et al. 2025) gives all matrices equal element RMS. With decoupled decay at 10x (time constant ~1000 steps at peak LR), fc2's steady-state scale is proportional to its update size for consistently aligned directions (sqrt for noise directions), so this raises the MLP's residual writes 1.4-2x relative to attention writes. If the MLP writes are under-scaled, equalizing them lets each block apply larger per-token transformations, improving the pretrained policy that round 1 of expert iteration samples from. Opposing risk: a larger fc2 is less plastic under the frozen RL AdamW (relative step ~lr_RL/||W||), the mechanism credited for 069/070's gains, and a larger MLP write could crowd out citation attention in the residual stream.
expected_delta: -40 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central guess 0); pretraining steps within 2% of 070's 4784/4750/4776 (the change adds no kernels); final val loss within +-0.004 of 070's 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961; if the stronger-MLP mechanism holds, round-1 targets solved above 070's 200/324/206 on at least two of three seeds

arch.change: none versus 070-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 069-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (same as 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
